For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the green beans came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-green-beans" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-green-beans-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of green beans, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>59</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Houlihan et al. 2019</td><td>2</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>U.S. Food and Drug Administration 2024</td><td>4</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for green beans, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food" class="internal" data-slug="sources/houlihan2019-hbbf-whats-in-baby-food" data-no-cite-meta>Houlihan et al. 2019</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2024-toxic-elements-baby-food-compliance-2009-2024" data-no-cite-meta>U.S. Food and Drug Administration 2024</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach green beans

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach green beans comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Green beans, as sold from Ruschita (mining area R) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 350 µg/kg, against 70 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<a id="what-remains-unresolved-when-was-each-answer-reviewed-and-what-changed-in-this-version"></a>

Every source record that names green beans was decided on its content: 19 occurrence extracted, 19 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.

## Green beans FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-green-beans" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-green-beans" data-question="What heavy metals are found in green beans?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in green beans?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, As, Ba, Hg, Sr, Ti and Tl in green beans, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-green-beans" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-green-beans" data-question="How do heavy metals get into green beans?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into green beans?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, green beans from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than green beans from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Green beans, as sold from Moldova Noua (mining area M) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 190 µg/kg, against 70 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-green-beans" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-green-beans" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in green beans?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in green beans?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, green beans, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in WPRO (10 µg/kg) and the highest in SEARO (40 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For inorganic arsenic, the lowest regional median was in EURO (41.5 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (43 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-green-beans-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-green-beans-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in green beans is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in green beans is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 8 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Marín S, Pardo O, Sánchez A, Sanchis Y, Vélez D, Devesa V, Font G, Yusà V · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Assessment of metal levels in foodstuffs from the Region of Valencia (Spain)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 654-670</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Marín et al. 2018 reported inorganic arsenic at 1.4 µg/kg (mean) in green beans, as sold from Vegetables and fruits group, Region of Valencia TDS 2010-2011.<sup class="cite">[[sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span
